title: Regional Decision Tree Authoring Experience
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Objective: Build a guided, visually-oriented authoring experience in Console that lets customers construct routing decision trees for region selection, tier routing, and fallback model variants. The authoring surface should make common patterns (region-first, tier-blend, failover-to-quantized-variant) easy to express, validate policies against platform constraints, and provide a deterministic preview/simulation before save/rollout.

User problems: Users find current policy DSL intimidating and make mistakes that cause unexpected latency or unavailable traffic during failover. They want a UI that: (1) expresses routing semantics at a higher level, (2) surfaces validation errors and safe defaults, and (3) previews how sample traffic will route under edge cases.

Goals (MVP):
1) Decision tree stepper UI that represents routing checks (region, latency thresholds, tier membership, capacity) as nodes and edges.
2) Node types: Region-match, Tier-match, Latency-check, Model-variant-fallback, Percentage-split.
3) Inline validation linter: model-region compatibility, tier quotas, quantization availability, and cross-region data residency flags.
4) Preview simulator: run a small synthetic traffic set (customer-provided sample or system preset) and show per-request path, latency/cost estimate, and fallback events.
5) Export and save: convert decision tree to policy DSL JSON, show human-readable summary, and hook to rollout controls (canary targets, rollback).

Out of scope for MVP: full drag-and-drop canvas with unlimited nesting, advanced expression language, and AI-assisted auto-suggestions (deferred to follow-up).

Acceptance criteria:
- PM/Design-approved wireframes exist in Figma and stakeholders signed off.
- Frontend implements stepper + node palette, with node inspector for parameters.
- Linter rules run on save and in-editor with actionable messages.
- Preview shows at least 5 synthesized traffic traces and aggregated latency/cost deltas.
- Policy export matches existing policy DSL and passes backend policy parser unit tests.
- E2E tests validate validation messages, preview accuracy, and policy export.

Implementation notes: reuse policy-parser service (ENG-49210) for validation; frontend built in React with the existing Console components library; telemetry hooks (console.routing.editor) added for node-add, preview-run, and save. Work with Design to finalize microcopy for safety messages.

Security & compliance: the authoring flow should never persist customer sample traffic. Preview runs in ephemeral environment. If customers upload sample traffic, it is stored in an encrypted short-lived blob and deleted after preview run. Coordinate with Security for retention policy (see dependency SEC-1085).

Links & artifacts:
- Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/routing-decision-tree
- Confluence spec: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/DECT-Authoring+Spec
- Policy parser PR (reference): https://github.com/redwood-inference/policy-parser/pull/214
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Kapoor: Kickoff meeting with Design and Eng. Agreed to prioritize a stepper-based UX over a free-form canvas for MVP to reduce engineering surface and make validation straightforward.

2026-03-11 Marco Chen: Feasibility note from Eng — policy-parser already supports model->region compatibility checks; we need a small adapter to run quotas and tier checks. Estimated ~3 backend days (ENG-49210 referenced).

2026-03-12 Lina Perez (Design): Added low-fidelity flows to Figma. Raised concern about explaining percent-split semantics to users; proposed inline examples and 'preview' button as primary guardrail.

2026-03-12 Marcus Li (SRE): Suggested telemetry events for preview-run and preview-fail so we can track customer confusion and iterate. Also noted preview must have safe limits (max 1000 traces / 60s).
2026-03-13 Marco Chen: Implemented basic validation endpoint and posted initial test harness in GH (link above). Need UX for showing deterministic sample traces vs aggregated summary.

2026-03-14 Aisha: PM review — updated acceptance criteria for export format to match runtime-1.18 policy schema. Approved proceeding to implementation; created follow-up task PM-310110 for rollout automation integration.
